content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a method to denoise videos using realistic noise. Previous work had build a model based on AWGN, which is not realistic. Some other work used paired noisy-clean videos, which are very difficult to collect, and may not generalize across different camera model. This paper proposes a flexible noise generation model for blind denoising of videos.  Two key observations in the architecture design are: 1) downsampling reduces noise, 2) information from adjacent frames can help with denoising. Experiment shows limited improvement over the comparison, and a short ablation study is shown.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
This paper addresses an important problem that is often overlooked in the vision community: AWGN is far from being realistic.
The resulting model appears to outperform the competition. The model runs fast, and is able to recover detail that was not recovered by other techniques.


Weakness
My concern for this paper is that it lacks novelty, the real noise degradation model for unrealistic noise are not convincing, and the evaluation lacks realism the author hopes to address.

Novelty:
- The two insights into the modeling approach is 1) downsampling remove noise, 2) adjacent frames is useful for denoising. Neither of these are novel. It is well-known within the signal processing/image processing community that downsampling will reduce the level of noise due to averaging. The second insight is virtually used everywhere in the preceding work. DVDNet include some level of warping and averaging across frames.

Real noise degradation model:
- The process for which the camera processes images is well known. However, the step listed has little to do with such process. The author simply shuffles each step to generate random noise model, which is equally to be as unrealistic as AWGN. For example, it is possible that JPEG noise step comes before Gaussian noise, which is unlikely to happen in reality (JPEG does have some smoothing so it will reduce the amount of Gaussian noise somewhat). There are many work that can almost be used off-the-shelf to generate realistic noise, see for example Brook et al.’s “Unprocessing Images for Learned Raw Denoising” and Guo et al.’s “Toward convolutional blind denoising of real photographs”
- The distribution of noise value as shown in Fig 10-11 is not the best representation of realism. It may be better to find a real video and compare the result with the output of this pipeline.

Evaluation:
- Because the paper is premised on denoising realistic noise, the evaluation on AWGN (section 4.1) do not add much to the whole narrative. Additionally, the proposed model improves over the comparison (VRT) by a fraction of dB. It is unclear how much better the proposed technique is.
- The evaluation on real video is relatively limited. The datasets do not have the ground truth to compare to. Further, the city dataset was collected from YouTube. It is unclear how much additional processing was done to those videos to stylize, and what other process were applied that could cause additional degradation (e.g. scanning of films). In my opinion, this dataset does not represent the real noisy video well. There are other noisy-real video dataset out there that maybe more well-suited for the evaluation task at hand. For example: “PVDD: A Practical Video Denoising Dataset with Real-World Dynamic Scenes” by Xu et al, or “Supervised Raw Video Denoising with a Benchmark Dataset on Dynamic Scenes” by Yue et al.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Please see my strength/weaknesses section for comment on quality and novelty. I think the paper was clear enough to follow along. Reproducibility-wise, I do not see a promise of code or dataset, so it may be difficult to reproduce.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I find this paper to lack novel contribution and convincing solutions to existing problem (the practical noise model is not realistic). Please see my strength/weakness section for more detail.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors present a new network architecture for video denoising.
Additionally, they propose a method for simulating different types of video noise, which are then used for supervised training.
This way, they aim to produce a denoiser that is robust to various types of noise and cameras. 
The authors compare their method to a variety of baselines and achieve favourable results.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
* Video denoising is an important topic that his highly relevant for range applications in consumer electronics or science.
* I like the approach of randomly generating different types of noise and applying them consecutively.
* The method seems to perform well compared to its baselines.

Weaknesses:
* Despite the authors saying their network architecture is simple, I find it rather complex.
* The notation and explanation of the method could be improved. Verious aspects remain unclear for me after reading the paper (see below).
* Some of the experiments and arguments are not very clear, I suspect some of the figures and equations contain mistakes.
* The language could be improved, by checking for typos.

Detailed Comments:
Figure 1 demonstrates the positive aspects of downscaling an image to remove noise.
I find this figure not very informative.
I don't really agree with the argument. It is true that downscaling (depending on how it is done) can remove noise.
If e.g. 4 pixels are combined to one, pixel-independent Gaussian noise will be reduced by averaging. However, we are also loosing details by reducing the size of the image, and downscaling is not generally helpful.
I believe there is an error in the plot showing PSNR values as a function of downscaling. The values are identical in all cases between 2x and 4x downscaling. 4x downscaling should be better, because it averages 16 pixels instead of only 4.

Regarding the plot that shows PSNR as a function of time,
is this looking only at single pixels? If this is the case, the plot is simply showing independent Gaussian noise, which fluctuates. It is not the noise level that goes up and down.

Notation, correctness of derivation:
The variable sigma is introduced as the standard deviation of the Gaussian. Later it seems to describe the parameters of the artificial noise pipeline. Is this correct?
If this is the case, I am afraid I cannot follow Eq. 8. On the left hand side of the equation, there is an expected value over the possible values for sigma, but on the right hand side it seems to be a fixed for eta(z_sigma). 
The proof for this in the supplement seems to use an notation using at times y as the clean image instead of x, and x instead of x_sigma for the noisy image.
What exactly is eta?

Is the spacial encoding the same as the downsampling operation?
It seems so, because of Eq. 2 (assuming that s is the scale). If so, why is this not said explicitly?



Typos:
"their performance would deteriorateS..."
"there ARE little work devoted to..."
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
I believe the paper is novel.
Unfortunately, the paper lacks a little in clarity. This makes the reproducibility questionable.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Unfortunately, I cannot recommend the paper for acceptance in its current state.
Many things are unclear and I think it would take considerable effort to clarify all these points.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 4: The contributions are significant, and do not exist in prior works.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new noise degradation model and a new real-world video denoising test dataset consisting of different real-world noises. The authors design a simple but effective real video denoising network by exploiting the inherent properties of a noisy video. Quantitative and qualitative experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: The results are better than sota denoising methods. 
                The proposed denoising test sets and noise degradation model are beneficial for the development of real world denoising. 

Weaknesses: 
 1.	The proposed degradation model is very similar to which proposed in Real-ESRGAN. It is necessary to compare them and give more analysis.

2.	Downscaling and utilizing neighboring frames are common in many image/video denoising papers. The key module in proposed network is the flow-guide DCN which is proposed in BasicVSR++. The novelty is a bit incremental.

3.	Since DCN and transformer modules have not well speed-optimized in most hardwares, it is better to also give flops comparison between different methods.

4.	The comparison in real video denoising lacks some competitive video denoising methods like fastdvdnet, VRT .

[1] Real-ESRGAN: Training Real-World Blind Super-Resolution with Pure Synthetic Data (2021 ICCVW)
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The novelty of this work is a bit incremental. 
First, the data synthesis method is very similar to Real-ESRGAN. 
Second, the main novelty of the proposed network is the U-net based structure and the multiscale flow-guided dcn. 
Although these strategies are not utilized in BasicVSR++, the multiscale operations are very common in image denoising.
content.summary_of_the_review: Considering the limited novelty, I recommend weak rejection.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, authors propose a multi-scale recurrent architecture based on two observing characteristics and construct a novel synthetic real noise degradation model by randomly shuffling different noise typoes to trian a denoising model. In the experimental part, the proposed method outperforms other baselines in both quantitative and qualitative comparisons, which verifies the effectiveness of the method. This paper is well writing and origanized. While, the contribution of the paper is limited and seems to be increamental. Besides several contribution of the proposed model is not well verified.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

1. The motivation of the paper is interesting and meaningful.
2. The paper is well writing and organized.

Weakness & Concerns:

1. I am wondering the connection between two observations and ReViD, especially those designs which are different from BasicVSR++? 
2. It would be better to replace learnable downscale convolutional layer with traditional ones to verify its effectiveness in ablation study. Besides, PSNR of downscaling three times on DAVIS is higher than ReViD, and thus should be shown in boldface.
3. What are the differences between the proposed degradation model and the one proposed in SCUNet[1]? Which details in design are specific for the video denoising? In RealBasicVSR, the proposed degradation model seems to consider sequence relationship by the proposed random walk. What are the advantages of the proposed degradation model and the one in RealBasicVSR?
4. How to prove that the proposed synthetic real noisy images are similar to the real ones? Could authors make comparisons between synthetic and real noisy images in the distribution like Figure 10?
5. Figure needs to be improved, e.g., black arrows mislead authors to think x2 near flows and x4 flows will be sent into temporal denoising block as previous and denoised feature respectively in Figure 4.



[1] Zhang K, Li Y, Liang J, et al. Practical blind denoising via swin-conv-unet and data synthesis[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2203.13278, 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity

The method is clearly presented and easy to understand.

Quality

Besides the weaknesses mentioned above, the overall quality of this paper is good.

Novelty

The novelty of the paper seems to be limited, the proposed network and degradation model seems to be increamental as mentioned in above.

Reproducibility

Methods presented in the paper is easy to reproduce.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper is well writing and organized. While, there are not clear demonstrations of the differences between this paper and previous work, thus it seems to be incremental and with limited contributions. Experimental parts also need to be improved. Under above considerations, I would recommend reject this paper unless concerns are well demonstrated.
